comment: The title of a terminal from its output (D-360). The output comes in pieces; reads gives, for each piece in order, the last title that ended in it, or null. A title is OSC 0 or OSC 2 and ends with a bell or with an escape and a backslash; other commands of the operating system are no title. A title over 1024 characters is not one. In the pieces, \u001b is the escape and \u0007 the bell. claude is how a title of Claude Code reads (spike 2026-10): the star waits for input, a turning mark means a turn goes on; name is what the session takes as its name, null while Claude Code does not know the subject.

reads.name: OSC 2 ends with an escape and a backslash
the last of two titles in one piece
other commands and sequences are no title
a new escape sequence cuts a command short

long.comment: A title of length characters x, then a bell.
